newsitem.title: INDIA: Four suspected Kashmir rebels killed in gunbattle.
newsitem.headline: Four suspected Kashmir rebels killed in gunbattle.

text.p: Indian paramilitary troops killed four suspected rebels on Monday in a gunbattle in the troubled region of Kashmir, police said.

But witnesses said at least two of the dead men were innocent civilians killed by the Border Securty Force (BSF) in retaliation for a guerrilla attack on a police patrol in Srinagar, summer capital of India's state of Jammu and Kashmir.
"They killed two innocent people in retaliatory fire after a police patrol was attacked with a grenade," witness Sumera Baba told Reuters.
The grenade exploded but caused no damage.
Indian police denied the charge and said all the four killed in the battle in Srinagar's Firdous Chowk area were militants.

"Militants fired upon a security force picket and lobbed a grenade at a security patrol. The fire was returned by the security forces and in the encounter, three militants were killed," a police spokesman said.
The fourth wounded militant died in a military hospital, he said.
Witnesses said the the Firdous Chowk area was tense after the gunbattle during a cordon-and-search operation by paramilitary troopers.
A BSF spokesman said the search operation was continuing.

The latest attack comes two days before Pakistani Foreign Minister Gohar Ayub Khan and his Indian counterpart Inder Kumar Gujral are scheduled to meet to try to resolve outstanding bilateral issues, including the hotly disputed issue of Kashmir.
The two countries have fought two of their three wars over the territory since both became independent from Britain 50 years ago.
The foreign secretaries ended four days of talks on March 31 and agreed to hold a subsequent round in Islamabad.
India controls two-thirds of Kashmir and accuses Moslem Pakistan of arming and training separatist guerrillas fighting New Delhi's rule in the state.

Pakistan, which rules the remaining one-third, says it only provides the separatists with political and diplomatic support. More than a dozen militant groups are fighting New Delhi's rule for Kashmir's independence or merger with neighbouring Pakistan.
Both Pakistan and Kashmir are overwhelmingly Moslem while India is mainly Hindu.
Police and hospitals say more than 20,000 people have been killed in the seven-year-old rebellion in the Himalayan region.
